changes: Security: admin pages escaped names, notes and titles without their quotes, which let a stored value run script in an administrator's browser; every page's escaping is fixed.
Fixed a mass edit of lines, MAGs or Enigmas with Expiry ticked and no date: it expired every selected line.
Fixed a backup restore whose database connection dropped mid-migration: it could reconnect to the live database and clear its tables.

Resellers: the REST table actions answered null, the guide listed streams outside the reseller's packages, sub-reseller secrets were returned, and credit transfers were logged with the wrong amount; all fixed. A package with unredeemed activation codes can no longer be deleted.

Admin permissions: bulk stream actions, the global search, the category templates, Stream Review and the dashboard graph now follow the group's permissions; a read-only API token no longer receives secret settings.
Blocked IPs accepts IPv4 ranges (/16 to /31). The MAG Scan settings page now saves and applies its lists. An alert held back by the quiet period is sent once the period ends.
IP matching for 'restrict same IP' now compares subnets for IPv6 too (any two IPv6 addresses counted as the same subnet).

A module installed or enabled from the panel gets its cron jobs at once, without a restart (the anti-abuse shield and its honeypot ports never started). A renamed module keeps its install, and an update that succeeds on a retry is no longer left Failed.

The segment gateway now also answers an MPEG-TS viewer's first request, creating its connection without a PHP request (needs an xc_fanout release with it; older daemons keep the first request on PHP).

Redis connection handler: a Redis restart no longer ends running TS, VOD and timeshift streams, the sweep no longer kills a worker that serves another viewer, and a panel with the handler off no longer connects to Redis on every viewer request.

Faster stream requests on large panels: the bouquets map is no longer decoded for every segment, key and playlist request, and cached lists are decoded once per process. Line lookup files no longer carry the username and password in their name.

Watch folders: Auto-Upgrade now works for a load balancer's folder scanned from MAIN (the load balancer must be updated too), and a copy that is kept is logged as DUPLICATE. An import with no TMDb title falls back to the folder's name.

Fixed the M3U review importing only the table page shown, a created channel losing its on-demand servers on edit, Enigma2 links always using http and unencoded credentials, a subtitle name with a space breaking a movie's start, and error pages being cached as images.
Bulk delete of streams now removes a stream taken off its last server, and a proxy action can no longer disable the main server.

Updates: a load balancer still on stable 2.3.9 (or a beta up to 2.4.x) can update to the betas again. Since 2.6.0 the setting it reads for its channel was missing, so it stayed on its release answering 'Already up to date'. Update MAIN first, then the load balancer.

Cluster: MAIN's connection-limit queue is bounded. A node asks about a line's limit on every request, and each request left a file in tmp; when requests outran the loop the files filled the temporary filesystem (over a million in one report). A viewer now has one file, old checks are dropped, and an admission that ran out no longer closes a viewer for a place nobody takes.
Legacy panel_api.php (when enabled) lists the line's categories and streams again; it answered the sign-in data only.
Episodes page: a link to a series' episodes now opens on that series (it listed every series'), and an episode whose file failed shows Down instead of 'On Demand' with a live play button.
Resellers: saving a MAG or Enigma device no longer removes the pairing an administrator made. The admin API's kill_connection now works with the Redis connection handler.

Install and update: the installer wrote config.ini (the database password) and its credentials files readable by everyone; they are now private, and an update closes config.ini on existing panels. The build checks the archives' file modes.
Dashboard: a 'Database ports' check warns while MariaDB and Redis on MAIN answer any address, with a pointer to the DB Allowlist setting.
